bib.title: MERLOT Reserve: Neural Script Knowledge through Vision and Language and Sound
bib.venue: preprint (arXiv:2201.02639v4, 13 May 2022; the PDF prints no venue)

read.skipped: References skimmed only; Fig 6 celebrity name list and Table 10/11 numeric columns are garbled in extraction and used only where legible.

question: Can a model learn joint representations of video frames, subtitles and audio with a self-supervised contrastive span objective, and do they transfer to fine-tuned and zero-shot vision-language tasks, including ones without sound?
hypothesis: Learning from all modalities in a time-locked, reentrant way (each modality teaching the others) gives better multimodal representations, and audio helps even audio-less tasks like VCR.
contributions: Reserve, a model for multimodal script knowledge, fusing vision, audio, and text.
A new contrastive span matching objective, enabling our model to learn from text and audio self-supervision.
Experiments, ablations, and analysis, that demonstrate strong multimodal video representations.

method.summary: Video is split into 5-second segments, each a middle frame plus either ASR text or audio. Independent ViT, AST and text-span encoders feed a bidirectional joint Transformer; 25% of text/audio subsegments are replaced by MASK and the model contrastively matches the MASK output to an independent encoding of the hidden span, plus a frame-to-transcript contrastive loss. Pretrained from scratch on YT-Temporal-1B, then fine-tuned on VCR, TVQA, Kinetics-600 or used zero-shot.
method.task: self-supervised multimodal video pretraining (contrastive masked span), then VCR, TVQA, Kinetics-600 fine-tuning and zero-shot STAR, EPIC-Kitchens, LSMDC, MSR-VTT QA

datasets.name: YT-Temporal-1B
datasets.size: 20 million English-subtitled YouTube videos, 1 billion frames
datasets.source: YouTube, video IDs only released, research use; built from 30M candidate IDs
datasets.preprocessing: filters: no gaming, dense speech (50 words in 30 s), cld3 English >=80%, thumbnail diversity, >=1 COCO object; no ASR clean-up; timing refined by MLP regressor trained on 2000 videos

datasets.name: The Pile (web text)
datasets.split: sequences of length 800 per video, 38 masked spans each

datasets.name: VCR
datasets.split: test via leaderboard; val for ablations

datasets.name: STAR, EPIC-Kitchens, LSMDC FiB, MSR-VTT QA

models.name: Reserve-B
models.architecture: ViT-B/16 + AST audio encoder + text span encoder + bidirectional joint Transformer
models.context: 640 tokens pretraining (8 segments), 1312 after res adaptation

models.name: Reserve-L
models.architecture: ViT-L/16 + AST + text span encoder + joint Transformer

other.zero_shot: logits averaged over frames, softmax over label space

models.name: UNITER-Large, VilBERT, VisualBERT, ERNIE-ViL, Villa, VATT, MTV, Just Ask

other.use: rewrites MSR-VTT QA questions into MASK statements, prompted with a dozen examples

training.objective: L = L_text + L_audio + L_frame; symmetric contrastive (CLIP-style) span matching with learned scale sigma clipped at 100; 25% of text/audio subsegments masked; two masked variants VT->TA and VTA->T
training.lr_schedule: linear warmup then cosine decay to 0.02x of max over 10 epochs; res adaptation: warm up to 0.02x peak over first 1/5 epoch then cosine to 0
training.batch_size: 1024 videos x N=16 segments (two groups of 8); 16384 frames for matching; 49152 text spans and 49152 audio spans
training.epochs: 10 (+1 for res adaptation; Reserve-L res adaptation 0.5 epoch after preemption)
training.precision: bfloat16, gradients and AdamW state in 16 bit, NaN gradients set to 0
training.regularisation: no dropout; weight decay 0.1 also applied toward pretrained weights when fine-tuning
training.compute: 5 days (B), 16 days (L) on TPU v3-512; roughly 3 weeks total, 20,000 kWh, 8.23 tCO2e

other.finetune_schedule: linear warmup over first half of first epoch, linear decay to 0
other.audio: 22050 Hz (table) / 22500 Hz (text), window 1536, hop 588, 64 mel bins, 1.6 s subsegments
other.loss_spikes: Reserve-L training loss sometimes spiked to near random init and recovered; cause unknown

inference.decoding: zero-shot: nearest label vector to MASK hidden state (no generation)
inference.samples: single run; no seeds or variance reported
inference.prompting: zero-shot: question converted to statement with MASK; N=8 segments; audio optional
inference.retrieval: label-space matching: MASK output vs encoded candidate phrases

parameters.TVQA_context: 35 s around annotated region; 7 further segments

metrics.definition: four-way multiple choice for answer, rationale, and both correct

limits: Authors: only learns from 40-second long videos, relies on ASR for subtitles, can only match (not generate) text and audio.
No seeds, variance or significance tests; all numbers single runs.
Reserve-L loss spikes during pretraining unexplained; larger model underperforms base on zero-shot STAR (attributed to limited prompt search).
TVQA audio gain over subtitles is 0.5 points on scripted dialogue; transcript carries most of the signal.
Zero-shot person recognition is weak (<11%), authors present this as a privacy benefit.
Inconsistencies: Table 7 lists VCR Q->AR 71.5 for Reserve-L vs 72.0 in Table 2; MSR-VTT label space 1k vs 2000; sample rate 22050 vs 22500 Hz.
No retrieval or RAG evaluation: this is a representation-learning paper.

terms.definition: Replace a span of text or audio with MASK and train the model to match the MASK representation to an independent encoding of the hidden span, versus others in the batch.
Time-locked correlations enable one modality to educate others.
